newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SAMPDORIA TITLE CONTENDERS AFTER MIRACLE WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SAMPDORIA TITLE CONTENDERS AFTER MIRACLE WIN.

text.p: Sampdoria firmly established themselves as Italian title contenders on Sunday, coming from behind to defeat Milan with 10 men at the San Siro -- a feat Milan president Silvio Berlusconi suggested was a miracle.
"We need to go to Lourdes to win a match like that," the grey-faced former prime minister told reporters.

Berlusconi had just watched his team recover from Roberto Mancini's first minute opener with two goals from Liberian George Weah, only to lose 3-2 to a side that had goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron sent off in the first half.
Late goals from Yugoslav Sinisa Mihajlovic and second-half substitute Marco Carparelli, who idolosed Milan's great Marco Van Basten as a boy, left Sampdoria just two points behind leaders Juventus.
It was the Genoa side's first victory at Milan since 1990, a year when they went on to take their only Italian title -- but Swedish manager Sven-Goran Eriksson ruled out title talk.

"We started the season with a dream -- to qualify for Europe," said Eriksson, commenting on Samp's seven-match unbeaten run, "I don't want to change that objective now. Any team that wins with 10 players is lucky."
The manner of Milan's eighth defeat of the season further undermined their dwindling reputation as invincible after recent home defeats by Parma and Norwegian side Rosenborg.
The crisis-hit side missed a host of gilt-edged opportunites as they dropped to seventh from bottom in the table.

"We must remain calm and try to bring the best out of our class players," said former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi, who has now lost four league matches since leaving the national side to coach Milan in December.
Victory stung all the more because Sacchi had fielded the same side that won the 1996-97 league title - although former Samp goalkeeper Angelo Pagotti took the out-of-form Sebastiano Rossi's place.
Ironically, it was Pagotto's error - miscontrolling a backpass - that left Roberto Mancini with an open goal in the first minute.
It was the Sampdoria captain's 139th in serie A - the highest among Italian strikers still playing - and probably the softest yet.
It shook Milan's confidence and they took 10 minutes to launch their first raid, the unmarked Zvonimir Boban shooting too close to Ferron.
Weah, out since Christmas with an ankle injury, went closer three minutes later, meeting Dejan Savicevic's dipping cross with a volley that scraped the bar.
In the 23rd minute, the match appeared to turn on the expulsion of Ferron, rightly shown the red card for hauling down Weah just outside the penalty area.

Replacement Matteo Sereni parried Roberto Baggio's freekick but there was nothing he could do about Weah's 37th minute equaliser, a firm shot from the edge of the six-yard box, after a weaving run by Yugoslavia's Savicevic.
It was the Liberian's eighth goal of the season and his first in the league since last October.
Soon after, Paolo Maldini, suffering the after-effects of flu, was substituted by Swede Jesper Blomqvist, giving Milan an extra attacker.

Milan should have turned round in front after Sereni saved Boban's 45th minute shot, and the ball fell to Weah three metres out -- but Mihajlovic miraculously saved the day with a spectacular goal-line clearance.
Instead the champions had to wait until the 57th minute to edge in front with a moment of brilliance from Weah.
The former European and World footballer of the year picked the ball up 35 metres out and unleashed a stunning shot into the top corner.
It should have sealed the match but Milan eased off and Samp's 10 men took heart.
Only an ever vigilant Franco Baresi stopped the ball crossing the line after an 68th minute goalmouth scramble.
But the veteran sweeper could only watch and despair as Mihajlovic curled a free kick beyond the reach of Pagotto from wide on the right in the 74th minute to level the scores.
Visibly encouraged, Samp pushed forward in search of a winner and in the 79th minute Carparelli was lurking to volley home after a miscued clearance by Alessandro Costacurta.

Milan's luck only looked like changing in injury-time when Savicevic rounded Sereni and rolled his ball toward the empty net but Oumar Dieng, whose only other match this season ended in a Samp win over Milan, got back to clear off the line.

From the resulting corner, Sereni, an Italy under-21 keeper, pulled off a blinding reflex save from Marcel Desailly's shot to make sure of a victory that launches Sampdoria as possible inheritors to Milan's league crown.

Teams: Milan: 25-Angelo Pagotto, 3-Paolo Maldini (34-Jesper Blomqvist 35th minute), 13-Francesco Coco, 6-Franco Baresi, 11-Alessandro Costacurta, 20-Zvonimir Boban (22-Edgar Davids 53), 8-Marcel Desailly, 4-Demetrio Albertini, 10-Dejan Savicevic, 18-Roberto Baggio, 9-George Weah (14-Michael Reiziger 73rd)

Sampdoria: 1-Fabrizio Ferron, 2-David Balleri, 7-Emanuele Pesaresi, 11-Sinisa Mihajlovic, 24-Oumar Dieng, 14-Christian Karembeu, 20-Juan Veron (25-Marco Carparelli 60th), 4-Marco Franceschetti (13-Giovanni Invernizzi 86th), 8-Pierre Laigle, 9-Vincenzo Montella (12-Matteo Sereni 23rd), 10-Roberto Mancini
